newsitem.title: UK: Blair wants to rid British streets of beggars.
newsitem.headline: Blair wants to rid British streets of beggars.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair never gives money to beggars and says he would be happier if they were cleared from the streets altogether.

But the homeless should be found somewhere to live and a Labour government would provide training so that they could get a job, he said in an interview with The Big Issue, a magazine sold by homeless people who keep part of the cover price.
"The basic principle here is to say: Yes, it is right to be intolerant of people homeless on the streets," Blair said in the interview, released on Tuesday.
"But the way to deal with that is you make sure that when those people come off the streets you're doing the other half of the equation," he added. "You're providing them with somewhere to go."

Labour, which looks likely to win general elections due by mid-May, has promised a comprehensive training programme for young people, paid for by a windfall tax on the profits of privatised utility companies.

Blair said it was appalling that some young people had to sleep in shop doorways and society should tackle the problem, but it was no solution to "give a pound or two to a beggar whenever we feel like it".
Blair was asked if he ever gave money himself to beggars.
"I don't, no," he replied. "I do buy The Big Issue occasionally, but I don't put that in the same category."
Blair backed "zero tolerance", the U.S. policy of cracking down on minor criminals, like graffiti artists, and other irritants in order to improve life in the towns and cities.

Labour's spokesman law and order, Jack Straw, has been attacked by left-wingers in the party for saying he wanted to clear the streets of beggars, addicts and "squeegee merchants" -- people who wash car windscreens at junctions and then ask for money, often aggressively.
Blair has shifted the party from the left towards the centre since becoming leader in 1994 and has frequently said that a Labour government would be "tough on crime and tough on the causes of crime".
